_meta.source: UK_IBD_Freebies_Discounts_Guide_2026.pdf (dated 1 Sep 2026), every claim re-checked against the live provider page on 2026-09-02

schema.integration_tier: 1 = provider form opens inside the hub (no X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors on the apply URL, still needs a real-browser test because iframes get partitioned cookies); 2 = online form exists but refuses framing, open in a named popup window and track the hand-off; 3 = no online form (phone, post, PDF, at the venue, via your own water company or council); the hub can only prepare the person
schema.apply_type: online | phone | post | pdf | at-venue | at-booking | via-supplier | via-council | via-gp | in-account
schema.eligibility_signals: keys of the My Access Folder profile that make this scheme likely: pip | dla | adp | aa | carers_allowance | blue_badge | ccuk_member | access_card | stoma | uc | pension_credit | housing_benefit | low_income | water_meter | state_pension_age | employed | child_under_16 | region_*
schema.frameable: result of a HEAD/GET header probe on apply_url, 2026-09-02

schemes.title: RADAR key (free with Crohn's & Colitis UK membership)
schemes.value_summary: Free RADAR key (normally £5-£10) for new patient members
schemes.what_you_get: A RADAR key opening more than 9,000 locked accessible toilets across the UK. One free key per new patient member who ticks the box on the join form.
schemes.who_qualifies: New Crohn's & Colitis UK members who are patients, or parents/carers of a patient, and request the key on sign-up. One per member while stock lasts.
schemes.ibd_note: Urgent toilet access is the most directly useful day-to-day benefit for Crohn's and colitis.
schemes.corrections: PDF linked the generic membership-benefits page; the eligibility wording lives on /radar-key. Add 'tick the RADAR key box on the join form; one per member'.

schemes.title: Can't Wait Card
schemes.value_summary: Discreet toilet-access card, included with membership
schemes.what_you_get: A card that lets you ask to use a toilet quickly without explaining. Combined with the membership card; available in 30 languages for travel.
schemes.who_qualifies: All Crohn's & Colitis UK members.
schemes.ibd_note: Useful for urgency and invisible symptoms. It is a request card: a business is not legally obliged to let you use its toilet.
schemes.corrections: 'Does not legally compel a business' is not on any CCUK page; keep it but attribute as general guidance. Add '30 languages'.

schemes.title: WaterSure capped water bill
schemes.value_summary: Water and sewerage bill capped at the company's average metered bill
schemes.what_you_get: Your metered bill is capped at the average bill for your area however much water you use. Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis are named as qualifying medical conditions.
schemes.who_qualifies: On a water meter (or an assessed charge where a meter cannot be fitted), a household member receiving a qualifying benefit (Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Housing Benefit, Income Support, income-based JSA/ESA and others), and either a named medical condition causing high water use or three or more children under 19 at home. Apply to your water company each year.
schemes.ibd_note: One of the few household-bill schemes that names Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis explicitly.
evidence_accepted: Medical practitioner's note (being dropped in the 2027 reform)
schemes.corrections: PDF cited a gov.uk news story about a reform that is NOT yet in force. Ofwat and CCW 'watersure' landing pages both 404; use the CCW FAQ or Citizens Advice. No central form: each supplier has its own, so the hub needs a postcode-to-water-company lookup.
schemes.upcoming_change: Reform legislated after the March 2026 consultation, due early 2027 (mandatory in England, voluntary in Wales): extends to households on a disability benefit with income under £25,745, caps at the lower of average metered/average bill, adds a single-occupier cap, removes the medical note requirement.

schemes.title: CEA Card: free cinema companion ticket
schemes.value_summary: One free companion ticket per visit at about 90% of UK cinemas
schemes.what_you_get: Buy your own ticket and the person accompanying you gets in free. The companion can help with moving around, emergencies, refreshments and toilet use.
schemes.who_qualifies: Automatic with PIP, DLA, Attendance Allowance, Scottish ADP/CDP/PADP, AFIP, or sight-impairment registration. Individual applications considered where accompaniment is needed because of disability. Minimum age 5.
schemes.ibd_note: Relevant where urgency, fatigue or treatment side-effects mean help may be needed during a visit.
schemes.corrections: All claims confirmed. Postal route also exists (/postal-application).

schemes.title: National Trust: one or two companions free
schemes.value_summary: Up to two carers or companions enter free with a disabled visitor
schemes.cost: Free (you still pay your own entry or membership)
schemes.what_you_get: One or two companions admitted free. The Essential Companion pass makes it quicker but is not required.
schemes.who_qualifies: Visitors who need one or two carers or companions. No proof requested at the gate.
schemes.ibd_note: Valuable for couples or families where the person with IBD needs support on days out.
schemes.apply_contact: 0344 800 1895 / enquiries@nationaltrust.org.uk / National Trust, PO Box 7083, Stratford-upon-Avon CV37 1XE
schemes.corrections: All confirmed. Page sits behind a Radware bot check: automated link monitors will report it blocked although it loads for people. Whitelist it in the link checker.

schemes.title: English Heritage: free essential companion
schemes.value_summary: Assisting companion enters free, no proof asked
schemes.what_you_get: Free site access for the assisting companion of a disabled member or visitor. The companion need not be a registered carer or the same person each visit.
schemes.who_qualifies: Where an assisting companion is needed to make the visit possible.
schemes.ibd_note: No evidence required, so the lowest-friction companion scheme on the list.
schemes.apply_contact: Select the 'essential companion' ticket when booking; letter of authority by phone 0370 333 1181
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. Add the 'select essential companion ticket when booking' route from the Visit FAQs. Do not add 'up to two' (third-party claim, not on the EH page).

schemes.title: Merlin attractions: free companion ticket + Ride Access Pass
schemes.value_summary: One complimentary companion ticket at Alton Towers, Thorpe Park, LEGOLAND, SEA LIFE and others
schemes.what_you_get: One free companion ticket for guests who need support. Ride Access Pass for guests who cannot queue.
schemes.who_qualifies: Evidence: PIP/DLA letters, Attendance or Carer's Allowance documentation, Blue Badge, CVI, or an Access Card with the +1 symbol.
schemes.ibd_note: Check each attraction's process. Companion tickets are usually issued in person at the ticket office; some attractions allow pre-booking.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. The companion ticket itself is in person; the free Merlin Digital Access Pass (needed for Ride Access Pass, ~72h processing) is an online Nimbus form with no framing headers, so it can open inside the hub.

schemes.title: Chessington: free carer ticket
schemes.value_summary: One free carer ticket per eligible guest
schemes.what_you_get: One free carer ticket (carer must be over 14); a second carer needs a GP/NHS letter. Ride Access Pass via the Merlin app from February 2026, applied for online at least 7 days before the visit.
schemes.who_qualifies: Accepted supporting documentation as listed on the Chessington accessibility page.
schemes.ibd_note: Carer tickets cannot be pre-booked and must be collected in person.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed.

schemes.title: Madame Tussauds London: free carer ticket
schemes.value_summary: Free carer ticket added during online booking
schemes.what_you_get: One carer ticket free of charge, added to your basket when buying a standard, Fast Track or multi-attraction ticket online. Documents checked at entry.
schemes.who_qualifies: Access Card, Blue or Orange Badge, DLA/PIP, Attendance or Carer's Allowance letter, Incapacity Benefit, CVI/BD8, or international proof of disability.
schemes.ibd_note: A mainstream commercial attraction with the companion freebie built into checkout.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. Ticket pages send no framing headers but a checkout with payment must not run inside our iframe; open in a popup.

schemes.title: London Zoo: disabled concession + free carer
schemes.value_summary: Concession ticket plus one essential carer free
schemes.what_you_get: Disabled adult and child ticket rates, plus one free carer ticket allocated at the gate on request.
schemes.who_qualifies: Supporting documents where a carer is needed: DLA letter, National Disability Card, local authority documents, Access Card.
schemes.ibd_note: Double saving: concession ticket plus free carer.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. Site refuses non-browser user agents (403): the link checker must send a browser UA.

schemes.title: Kew Gardens: concession + free essential companion
schemes.value_summary: Concession ticket (peak £23 online / £26 gate) plus companion free
schemes.what_you_get: Free daytime entry for essential companions, personal assistants, support workers and next of kin accompanying disabled visitors. Disabled visitors pay the concession rate. Daytime visits only; ticketed evening events need full-price tickets.
schemes.who_qualifies: Where an essential companion is needed; ID may be requested for the concession.
schemes.ibd_note: Accessible toilets on site.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. Add 'daytime only' and the peak concession price. Site 403s non-browser UAs.

schemes.title: RHS Gardens: free companion
schemes.value_summary: One companion free at RHS gardens
schemes.what_you_get: One companion admitted free for each wheelchair user, visually impaired visitor, or visitor whose disability necessitates a carer. Ticket issued at the garden entrance.
schemes.who_qualifies: Where the disability necessitates a carer.
schemes.ibd_note: Worth checking where IBD symptoms create a genuine need for assistance. RHS shows differ: Chelsea companion tickets are requested by phone (0333 300 3015) at purchase.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed (the cited page is the T&C page). Also cite https://www.rhs.org.uk/accessibility.

schemes.title: Cadw (Wales): disabled visitor and companion both free
schemes.value_summary: Free entry for the disabled visitor and one companion at all Cadw sites
schemes.what_you_get: All disabled people are admitted free and can bring one companion free. Ask staff if you need more than one. Optional free Disabled Person's Membership card includes the companion.
schemes.who_qualifies: Disabled visitors, explicitly including non-visible impairments. No evidence requirement stated.
schemes.ibd_note: Unusually generous: both the visitor and the companion are free.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. Add /visit/places-to-visit/admissions/disabled-people for the free membership card.

schemes.title: Disabled Persons Railcard
schemes.value_summary: 1/3 off most rail fares for you and one adult companion
schemes.what_you_get: A third off most adult rail fares for the holder and one adult travelling with them. Can be loaded onto a registered Oyster card for 1/3 off pay-as-you-go Tube, DLR and National Rail fares (holder only).
schemes.who_qualifies: PIP or ADP award letter; DLA/CDP; Attendance Allowance; visual or hearing impairment; epilepsy; War Pensioner's Mobility Supplement; Motability; since 1 March 2026 also a Disabled Persons Bus Pass or Freedom Pass, or being unable to drive on medical grounds; AFCS; Industrial Injuries 20%+.
schemes.ibd_note: The 2026 widening matters: many people with IBD hold a bus pass or a Blue Badge but not PIP.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. Add the March 2026 eligibility additions. Online purchase needs evidence upload (JPEG/PDF up to 4 MB) and a passport-style photo; postal PDF exists; phone 0345 605 0525.

schemes.title: Disabled Person's Bus Pass
schemes.provider: Your local council (English National Concessionary Travel Scheme)
schemes.value_summary: Free local bus travel, currently 9.30am to 11pm weekdays and all weekend; 24/7 from 1 April 2027
schemes.what_you_get: Free off-peak local bus travel anywhere in England. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland run their own schemes.
schemes.who_qualifies: Disability-based, assessed by the local council; an IBD diagnosis alone is not an automatic route.
schemes.ibd_note: Worth checking where IBD causes qualifying mobility or other substantial limitations. Since March 2026 the pass also unlocks the Disabled Persons Railcard.
schemes.corrections: 'Off-peak' is not on the gov.uk page; the times and the April 2027 change come from the GOV.UK news release of 17 August 2026. Apply via the council found through the gov.uk postcode lookup.
schemes.upcoming_change: Free travel at any time of day from 1 April 2027 (GOV.UK, 17 Aug 2026).

schemes.title: Blue Badge
schemes.value_summary: Parking concessions closer to your destination
schemes.cost: Up to £10 in England, £20 in Scotland, free in Wales; lasts up to 3 years
schemes.what_you_get: Parking concessions that make it easier to park near where you are going.
schemes.who_qualifies: Automatic with DLA higher-rate mobility, PIP 8+ points for moving around or 10 points descriptor E for planning journeys, registered blind, War Pensioners' Mobility Supplement or AFCS tariffs 1-8. Everyone else is assessed on how journeys between vehicle and destination are affected, including non-visible conditions.
schemes.ibd_note: IBD does not guarantee a badge, but severe pain, urgency-driven journey limits or mobility effects may be relevant.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. Add the fee and validity from gov.uk/apply-blue-badge.

schemes.title: Access Card (Nimbus)
schemes.value_summary: Recognised access card; the WC symbol means urgent toilet access without question
schemes.cost: £15 for 3 years (free Digital Access Pass also available)
schemes.what_you_get: A card that translates your needs into symbols venues recognise. WC = urgent toilet needs; +1 = essential companion. Accepted by Merlin, Madame Tussauds, London Zoo, Kew and many others.
schemes.who_qualifies: Assessed on evidence of substantial, significant or frequent needs, not diagnosis alone.
schemes.ibd_note: The urgent-toilet symbol is the single most IBD-relevant feature on this list, and the card unlocks companion tickets across the days-out schemes.
evidence_accepted: Consultant or GP letter describing functional impact
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. Price and validity added. The application app sends no framing headers, so this is the strongest candidate for an on-hub sign-up.

schemes.title: Personal Independence Payment (PIP)
schemes.value_summary: Weekly: daily living £76.70 or £114.60; mobility £30.30 or £80.00 (2026/27)
schemes.what_you_get: Tax-free disability benefit paid whether or not you work or have savings. A PIP award unlocks most of the other schemes here (CEA Card, Railcard, Blue Badge, companion tickets, vehicle tax).
schemes.who_qualifies: A long-term condition causing difficulty with everyday tasks or getting around, for 3 months already and expected to last at least 12 more. Scotland uses Adult Disability Payment.
schemes.ibd_note: Assessed on functional impact, not diagnosis: continence, fatigue, pain, treatment burden and mobility all count.
schemes.apply_contact: 0800 917 2222 (Mon-Fri 8am-5pm); online only in some postcodes; Scotland: mygov.scot/adult-disability-payment
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. 'Tax-free' is on /how-much-youll-get rather than the cited page. Rates added.

schemes.title: Attendance Allowance
schemes.what_you_get: Regular financial support for people over State Pension age who need help with personal care or supervision.
schemes.who_qualifies: Over State Pension age and needed the help for at least 6 months; faster, higher-rate route for people nearing the end of life (form SR1).
schemes.ibd_note: Relevant to older people with severe IBD-related care needs.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. Online claim service now exists; rates added.

schemes.title: Universal Credit health element (LCWRA)
schemes.value_summary: £429.80 a month (higher rate) or £217.26 (lower rate, claims from 6 April 2026)
schemes.what_you_get: Extra Universal Credit where a health condition limits capability for work. Since 6 April 2026 there are two rates: higher for pre-April claimants, severe lifelong conditions or end of life; lower for new claims.
schemes.who_qualifies: Depends on household circumstances and the Work Capability Assessment. Report the condition in your UC journal with a fit note.
schemes.ibd_note: Income support rather than an IBD-specific discount.
schemes.corrections: 6 April 2026 change confirmed. Amounts are NOT on the cited page; they come from gov.uk/universal-credit/what-youll-get and must be cited from there.
schemes.upcoming_change: Lower LCWRA rate frozen until April 2030.

schemes.title: NHS Low Income Scheme (HC2/HC3)
schemes.value_summary: Full or partial help with prescriptions, dental, eye care, travel to appointments, wigs and fabric supports
schemes.what_you_get: An HC2 (full help) or HC3 (partial help) certificate.
schemes.who_qualifies: Low income with capital under £16,000 (£23,250 if permanently in a care home). Apply online only if capital is £6,000 or less; otherwise the paper HC1.
schemes.ibd_note: Useful for people facing repeated healthcare costs, and it unlocks the travel costs scheme.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. Add the £6,000 online-only threshold. nhsbsa.nhs.uk returns 403 to non-browser fetchers.

schemes.title: Healthcare Travel Costs Scheme
schemes.value_summary: Refund of travel costs to NHS specialist appointments
schemes.what_you_get: Refund of the cheapest suitable travel (public transport, mileage, parking, tolls, pre-arranged taxi, congestion charge) to referred specialist treatment or tests. Claim within 3 months.
schemes.who_qualifies: A qualifying benefit or an HC2/HC3 certificate, plus a referral to specialist care.
schemes.ibd_note: Covers gastroenterology and IBD clinic visits where the criteria are met.
schemes.apply_contact: In person at the hospital cashiers' office on the day, or post form HC5(T)
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. No online form. nhs.uk page is past its August 2026 review date.

schemes.title: Prescription Prepayment Certificate (England)
schemes.value_summary: £32.05 for 3 months or £114.50 for 12 months (10 direct debits of £11.45); single items are £9.90
schemes.what_you_get: Covers all NHS prescriptions in the period. Saves money from the second item a month.
schemes.who_qualifies: Anyone paying for prescriptions in England.
schemes.ibd_note: Crohn's and ulcerative colitis are not on the medical exemption list, so most people with IBD pay. A permanent stoma (ileostomy or colostomy) IS on the list: ask your GP for form FP92A instead of buying a PPC.
schemes.corrections: Prices confirmed. Add the stoma exemption; it is the one free-prescription route open to part of this audience.

schemes.title: VAT relief on disability goods and services
schemes.value_summary: 0% VAT on qualifying goods designed for disabled or chronically sick people
schemes.what_you_get: Zero-rated purchase of products designed or adapted for personal or domestic use by a disabled or chronically sick person, plus their adaptation, repair and maintenance.
schemes.who_qualifies: A condition the medical profession treats as a chronic sickness. The goods must qualify in their own right; everyday items are not VAT-free because the buyer has IBD.
schemes.ibd_note: IBD can meet the chronic-sickness definition. Claimed by giving a written declaration to each supplier, not by applying to HMRC.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed. Guidance page last updated 2019. The hub can pre-fill the declaration PDF from the member's profile.

schemes.title: Vehicle tax exemption or 50% reduction
schemes.value_summary: 100% exemption with enhanced-rate mobility PIP or higher-rate mobility DLA; 50% off with standard-rate mobility PIP
schemes.what_you_get: Full exemption for one vehicle at a time (higher-rate mobility DLA, enhanced-rate mobility PIP/ADP, War Pensioners' Mobility Supplement, AFIP) or a 50% reduction (standard-rate mobility PIP/ADP).
schemes.who_qualifies: Holders of the listed mobility awards; the vehicle must be used by or for the disabled person.
schemes.ibd_note: Only relevant where the person also holds a qualifying mobility award.
schemes.apply_contact: First claim at a Post Office that handles vehicle tax (or the dealership for a new car); 50% reduction by post to DVLA, Swansea SA99 1BF
schemes.corrections: The cited page lists neither the qualifying benefits nor the 50% route; cite gov.uk/financial-help-disabled/vehicles-and-transport instead.

schemes.title: Access to Work
schemes.value_summary: Grant for workplace equipment, support workers, travel to work and adjustments
schemes.what_you_get: Pays for practical support at work: specialist equipment, support workers, travel where public transport is unusable, vehicle adaptations, workplace changes and mental-health support.
schemes.who_qualifies: Aged 16+, in England, Scotland or Wales, in paid work or starting within 12 weeks, with a condition that affects doing the job or getting to it.
schemes.ibd_note: Complements the employer's duty to make reasonable adjustments: a nearer parking space, a private toilet route, home-working equipment.
schemes.corrections: Confirmed.

schemes_additional.title: Council Tax Disabled Band Reduction Scheme
schemes_additional.provider: Your local council (Disabled Band Reduction Scheme)
schemes_additional.value_summary: Council tax charged at the band below yours (Band A properties get 17% off instead)
schemes_additional.what_you_get: Your bill is worked out as if the property were in the next band down (e.g. a Band D home is billed at Band C rates). Band A properties get a 17% discount instead, since there's no band below A.
schemes_additional.who_qualifies: A disabled person (adult or child, not necessarily the bill payer) must live in the property, which must have an extra bathroom, kitchen or other room needed for the disabled person, or extra indoor space to use a wheelchair. Applies whether or not the household also gets Council Tax Reduction (the separate means-tested discount).
schemes_additional.ibd_note: Relevant where a stoma, severe urgency or mobility needs have led to home adaptations, e.g. a downstairs shower room or wet room built for faster or easier toilet access.
evidence_accepted: Occupational therapist report (helpful but not always required)
schemes_additional.corrections: Verified live on gov.uk (England) 2026-09-03: reduces the bill to the band below, or 17% off for Band A; qualifying room/wheelchair-space wording quoted directly from the page. Wales runs the same scheme through gov.wales and local councils; Scotland's local authorities apply the same criteria (and a Scottish award can also unlock up to 35% off water/waste charges, not covered by this entry). Northern Ireland has no council tax; it is out of scope.

schemes_additional.title: Motability Scheme
schemes_additional.provider: Motability Operations (overseen by the Motability charity)
schemes_additional.value_summary: Exchange your mobility allowance for a leased car, Wheelchair Accessible Vehicle, scooter or powered wheelchair
schemes_additional.cost: Your mobility allowance is paid across to Motability; many cars need no extra Advance Payment, some need one on top
schemes_additional.what_you_get: A new car, Wheelchair Accessible Vehicle, scooter or powered wheelchair on a lease that bundles insurance, servicing, tyres, breakdown cover and (for cars) an annual mileage allowance, paid for by signing over your mobility allowance for the lease term.
schemes_additional.who_qualifies: Enhanced-rate mobility component of PIP, higher-rate mobility component of DLA, enhanced-rate mobility component of Adult Disability Payment (Scotland), higher-rate mobility component of Child Disability Payment (Scotland), War Pensioners' Mobility Supplement, or Armed Forces Independence Payment, with at least 12 months left on the award when you apply.
schemes_additional.ibd_note: Only relevant to the minority of people with IBD whose functional impact (e.g. severe fatigue, joint disease, or a stoma with mobility complications) is enough to secure an enhanced/higher-rate mobility award; standard-rate PIP mobility does not qualify.
evidence_accepted: PIP/DLA/ADP award letter showing enhanced or higher mobility rate and remaining award length
schemes_additional.apply_contact: 0300 456 4566 (Mon-Fri 8.30am-6pm, Sat 9am-1pm); joining is completed with a participating dealer once eligibility is confirmed
schemes_additional.corrections: Verified live on motability.co.uk 2026-09-03. The site sends a strict frame-ancestors CSP (only motability.co.uk/vercel/jotform/contentful) and, in any case, has no single online 'apply' step: eligibility is checked online, but the vehicle itself is chosen and ordered through a participating dealer. Non-qualifying benefits explicitly ruled out on the page: standard-rate PIP mobility, Attendance Allowance, Carer's Allowance, ESA.

schemes_additional.title: Disabled Facilities Grant
schemes_additional.value_summary: Council grant of up to £30,000 (England), £36,000 (Wales) or £25,000 (NI) for home adaptations
schemes_additional.cost: Free to apply; means-tested contribution possible for adults (not for disabled children, and not for landlords)
schemes_additional.what_you_get: Funding to adapt your home: widening doors, ramps, grab rails, stairlifts, level-access showers/wet rooms, improved garden access, extensions for an extra bedroom or bathroom, and heating/lighting controls you can reach and use. Getting the grant does not affect any other benefits.
schemes_additional.who_qualifies: Disabled people needing adaptations to remain living safely and independently at home, assessed by the council (usually via an occupational therapist visit first). For adults the amount can depend on household income and savings over £6,000; under-18s are assessed without their parents' income being taken into account; landlords are not means-tested.
schemes_additional.ibd_note: Covers building a downstairs or en-suite toilet/shower room, widening a bathroom doorway, or other adaptations that make urgent, frequent toilet access realistic at home.
schemes_additional.corrections: Verified live on gov.uk 2026-09-03: maximum amounts and means-test rules for England/Wales/NI quoted directly from the page. Scotland does not offer this grant; it runs its own, differently structured adaptations funding through local authorities, not covered by this entry.

schemes_additional.title: Warm Home Discount
schemes_additional.provider: Your electricity supplier (scheme run by DESNZ/Ofgem)
schemes_additional.value_summary: One-off £150 discount off your electricity bill
schemes_additional.what_you_get: A one-off £150 reduction applied directly to your electricity account by your supplier for the winter (2026/27 scheme year). Prepayment-meter customers get a voucher instead of a bill credit; the money is never paid directly to you.
schemes_additional.who_qualifies: You (or your partner) receive Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Housing Benefit, or income-related Employment and Support Allowance, your name (or your partner's) is on the electricity bill, and your supplier is part of the scheme. From the 2026/27 scheme year the separate 'high cost to heat' property score has been removed, so every household on one of those benefits qualifies, not just those in poorly-insulated homes.
schemes_additional.ibd_note: Not IBD-specific, but relevant because Universal Credit's health/LCWRA element and income-related ESA (both already common among people whose IBD limits work) are qualifying benefits in their own right.
schemes_additional.apply_contact: Most households are matched automatically by DWP/HMRC data and don't need to apply; if you think you qualify but haven't heard anything, call the Warm Home Discount helpline on 0800 030 9322 (Mon-Fri, 8am-6pm)
schemes_additional.corrections: Verified live on gov.uk 2026-09-03 across the scheme overview and the 2026/27 England & Wales eligibility statement: removal of the high-cost-to-heat threshold and the four qualifying benefits quoted directly from the official eligibility statement. Scotland runs a separate application-based route rather than automatic data-matching; not covered by this entry. Scheme showed as closed at verification time, due to reopen in October 2026 for winter 2026/27 payments.

schemes_additional.title: London Congestion Charge & ULEZ: disability discounts and exemptions
schemes_additional.value_summary: 100% exemption from the Congestion Charge, and (via time-limited grace periods) the ULEZ charge, for disabled drivers/vehicles in London
schemes_additional.cost: Free; Congestion Charge Blue Badge discount registration costs £10/year
schemes_additional.what_you_get: Congestion Charge: a Disabled Tax Class vehicle is automatically exempt with no registration needed; a Blue Badge holder can register (£10/year, renewed with the badge) up to two vehicles for a 100% discount. ULEZ: three separate time-limited 'grace periods' give a 100% discount to Disabled Tax Class vehicles, Wheelchair Accessible Vehicles, and holders of PIP/DLA/ADP/CDP mobility awards, War Pensioners' Mobility Supplement or AFIP (plus some medical-criteria routes) — each currently runs to October 2027, not indefinitely.
schemes_additional.who_qualifies: London drivers/passengers who are Blue Badge holders, hold a DVLA 'disabled' tax class vehicle, or receive a mobility-related disability benefit; both charges only apply inside their respective London zones.
schemes_additional.ibd_note: Only relevant to people with IBD who both drive/are driven in central or inner London and hold one of the qualifying benefits or a Blue Badge; the ULEZ routes are time-limited grace periods, not permanent exemptions.
evidence_accepted: Attendance Allowance award letter (state pension age route)
schemes_additional.corrections: Verified live on tfl.gov.uk 2026-09-03. Congestion Charge and ULEZ have separate rules: the Congestion Charge Disabled Tax Class exemption is permanent and automatic, the Blue Badge Congestion Charge discount needs a paid £10/year registration, and all three ULEZ disability grace periods are dated (24-25 October 2027) rather than permanent. Apply pages sit on tfl.gov.uk with X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, so they refuse framing.
schemes_additional.upcoming_change: All three ULEZ disability grace periods are due to end in October 2027 unless TfL extends them; after that, non-compliant vehicles driven by disabled people would need to pay the ULEZ charge like anyone else.

schemes_additional.title: Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA)
schemes_additional.provider: Student Finance England (equivalent bodies in Wales/Scotland/NI)
schemes_additional.value_summary: Non-repayable, non-means-tested funding for study-related costs caused by a disability or long-term health condition, up to £27,783/year
schemes_additional.cost: Free; you pay the first £200 towards a computer if one is recommended
schemes_additional.what_you_get: Funding for specialist equipment, non-medical helpers (e.g. a note-taker), taxi travel to your course or placement if public transport isn't possible because of your condition, and other disability-related study costs. It doesn't cover costs unrelated to your course, or things any student would need to pay for anyway.
schemes_additional.who_qualifies: Higher or further education students with a mental-health condition, long-term illness or disability whose needs are confirmed at a needs assessment; not means-tested and does not need to be paid back. Support is agreed after an eligibility letter, an assessment (in person or remote) with a DSA-approved assessor, and a report setting out what's approved.
schemes_additional.ibd_note: IBD can qualify as a long-term health condition; likely support includes ergonomic equipment, extra printing/travel costs around flares or hospital appointments, or specialist mentoring, agreed at the needs assessment rather than fixed in advance.
evidence_accepted: Evidence of disability/health condition (e.g. consultant letter)
schemes_additional.corrections: Verified live on gov.uk 2026-09-03; figures and process quoted directly from the page. This entry covers England-administered DSA; Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland run their own versions (via Student Finance Wales, SAAS, and Student Finance NI) with broadly similar but not identical rules, not verified here.

schemes_additional.title: Carer's Allowance
schemes_additional.value_summary: £86.45 a week for someone who cares for you at least 35 hours a week
schemes_additional.what_you_get: A weekly payment to whoever provides at least 35 hours a week of care for you (a family member, partner or friend, not necessarily living with you), plus National Insurance credits for them and possible knock-on entitlement to Council Tax Reduction, Universal Credit or Pension Credit.
schemes_additional.who_qualifies: The carer must spend 35+ hours a week caring and earn £204 or less a week after tax, NI and expenses. The person being cared for (i.e. the person with IBD) must already receive PIP daily living component, DLA middle/highest care rate, Attendance Allowance, Adult/Child Disability Payment, Pension Age Disability Payment or Armed Forces Independence Payment.
schemes_additional.ibd_note: This is a benefit for whoever cares for someone with severe IBD, not for the person with IBD directly — relevant where a partner, parent or adult child provides regular hands-on or supervisory care around flares, hospital admissions or fatigue.
evidence_accepted: The cared-for person's PIP/DLA/AA/ADP award letter
schemes_additional.corrections: Verified live on gov.uk 2026-09-03; rate, hours and earnings limit quoted directly from the page. This entry covers England, Wales and Northern Ireland only: since November 2024 Scotland has been transferring claimants to Carer Support Payment (fully replacing new Carer's Allowance claims there, with final transitional rules taking effect 15 March 2026), so gov.uk's Carer's Allowance no longer applies to new Scottish claims.

schemes_additional.title: Priority Services Register (energy and water suppliers)
schemes_additional.provider: Your energy and/or water supplier or network operator (Ofgem-regulated)
schemes_additional.value_summary: Free extra help from your energy/water supplier: priority support in a power cut, accessible bills, and more
schemes_additional.what_you_get: Priority support during power cuts or supply interruptions, advance warning of planned works, a password scheme so you can identify genuine supplier staff at your door, help reading meters or moving a prepayment meter, bills and information in large print, braille or another accessible format, and support if you rely on medical equipment that needs electricity.
schemes_additional.who_qualifies: Anyone disabled, chronically ill, of pension age, pregnant, with young children, or otherwise in a vulnerable situation. Self-declared: no proof of condition, age or situation is required.
schemes_additional.ibd_note: Worth having if IBD (or its treatment) means you depend on power for medical equipment, need extra notice before a planned outage affects medication storage, or would struggle with a phone-only process during a flare.
schemes_additional.apply_contact: Contact your electricity, gas and water suppliers/network operators individually (each requires its own registration; re-register if you switch supplier)
schemes_additional.corrections: Verified live on ofgem.gov.uk 2026-09-03; what's included and 'no proof required' quoted directly from the official page. Water companies run an equivalent 'Priority Services' offering regulated by Ofwat rather than Ofgem; Northern Ireland's equivalent is run separately by NIE Networks/the Utility Regulator. Neither is covered by the cited Ofgem page.
